gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-h: Groovy lopes in with a near-shut c slit and loosely spaced lowercase, all friendly and funky. Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau replies in plain sans curves that stay open, with capitals only a short step above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Loose, funky, and round-tipped as a marker. The strongest thing here is the gap in character: Groovy's pen-drawn heading letters sit above Noto Sans PhagsPa, whose see-through sans-serif curves feel modern and approachable.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-phoenicia: Chunky tubing letters with a grin. Noto Sans Phoenician takes over below with plain sans curves that open wide at both ends and a generous lowercase, so a long passage reads easily after Groovy's playful heading.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-psalter-p: Friendly is the first word for Groovy, whose c nearly seals itself shut. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi is the opposite, a plain sans with gaping e mouths, and shrinking the heading would blunt that closed-versus-open play.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Funky and monoline, Groovy keeps every stroke one gauge while its c all but closes up. Yet Noto Sans Rejang opens everything back out, with porthole-wide counters, and that closed-to-open turn is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Bouncy, tubular, and full of grin. Noto Sans Samaritan keeps a hefty lowercase with plenty of daylight inside its curves, so a long passage reads comfortably under Groovy's lively heading.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-saurashtr: Noto Sans Saurashtra reads as a plain sans whose capitals barely stand above their neighbors and whose counters stay linked to the outside. A longer passage feels smooth under Groovy's loud outline.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-sc: Noto Sans SC reads light, with curves stopping short of closing. Its quiet open shapes against Groovy's nearly shut c are the pair's strongest quality, one lively, one relaxed.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Groovy draws everything with one fixed nib width and a c that nearly seals. Noto Sans Sharada, a sans with open c forms and bulky lowercase, makes a longer passage feel sturdy and easy to follow.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham reads wide and approachable, with a big central band and an s whose ends hang far from the spine. Make the Groovy heading small and its closed shapes would fade beside that open sans.
